body_long:
Mandarin Oriental no longer has a Food & Beverage department. On 3 November 2026, the group announced that the function becomes Restaurants, Bars & Experiences, or RB&E. The idea is simple: restaurants and bars stop being hotel "outlets" and are run as destinations in their own right, where food, drink, design, music and culture meet.

## What changes

The group says its RB&E venues now hold 33 Michelin stars. Among them are The Bay by Chef Fei in Shenzhen and Jiang by Chef Fei in Guangzhou, with two stars each, and OPUS by Chef Alessio Durante in Shenzhen, with one. Alongside its chef partnerships, Mandarin Oriental is developing a small number of concepts and experience platforms it owns outright.

Hong Kong is the first showcase. The flagship on Connaught Road is reworking 14 restaurant, bar and experience venues in phases. The Pizza Bar by Daniele Cason, an Italian-Japanese pizza counter from Tokyo, and Thistle & Jade, a whisky salon designed by Malherbe Paris, were due to open on 2 November, with Blake Foyer to follow. In Europe, the group points to the four concepts at Mandarin Oriental Punta Negra in Mallorca, including Matsuhisa, to Le Sept and the Atelier 7 venues in Vienna, and to its collaboration with A. Wong at Mandarin Oriental Mayfair.

## The people behind it

The division is led by Christian Gradnitzer, Group Director RB&E. Born in Austria, he trained at Kurhotel Warmbaderhof in Carinthia, then worked at The Dorchester in London and for Cunard before joining Burj Al Arab in 2000. In 2014 he became corporate culinary director of Jumeirah's new restaurants and bars division, a structure close to the one he now leads. He later held senior food and beverage roles with Hilton and led Rikas Hospitality Group, before Mandarin Oriental appointed him Group Director of Food & Beverage in September 2025.

He is joined by James Norman, Regional Director of RB&E Operations for Europe and the Americas, who previously held senior roles with Ritz-Carlton, Kempinski and Mandarin Oriental. Gradnitzer sums up the approach in one line: "Craft differentiates us, but execution earns trust." He also presents RB&E as an investment in the careers of the group's teams.

## The signal

Renaming a department can look cosmetic. Here it comes with new leadership, owned concepts and a flagship transformation. For hoteliers, the lesson is that a hotel restaurant is now judged like any stand-alone address in town, by locals as much as by guests, and that the people who run it need a career path to match. Congratulations to the RB&E teams across the group.
